entries.title: Acts 8:5
segments: Philip. Not the apostle, but one of the seven deacons mentioned in

.  He now became an evangelist.
 

 
Samaria. The capital city of the province of that name.

entries.title: Acts 8:9
segments: Simon. A Samaritan by birth.  He was an indefatigable enemy of both Peter and Paul.  He was a sorcerer and conjurer.

entries.title: Acts 8:13
segments: Simon also himself believed. But it was not a sincere belief in Jesus Christ, whom Philip had preached to the people.  It was rather a belief in the superior power, which had made Philip a better worker of miracles than he (Simon), was.  The Samaritan conjurer was amazed and humiliated by one to whom the power of healing was after all but one of the consequences of his faith in the risen Christ.

entries.title: Acts 8:14
segments:
:17
 
Sent unto them Peter and John. In other words, they formally accepted the converted Samaritans as duly accredited followers of Jesus.  The new converts were considered by Jews almost as idolaters on account of their heathen origin.  It was the first step towards bringing the great outside world of Gentiles into the Christian church.

entries.title: Acts 8:18
segments: He offered them money. The hypocrisy and love of notoriety, which were at the bottom of Simon's 'belief', were revealed in this offer.  He had been waiting and watching all the time to learn the secret of Philip's power of working miracles.  It occurred to him that Philip might sell the secret.  The laying on of hands he evidently looked upon as a conjurer's trick.  His brazen materialism brought upon him a deserved rebuke.

entries.title: Acts 8:24
segments: Pray ye for me. A request, which at least implied a prudent fear of the Power, which had enabled Philip to do so much.  It went no further than that.  There was no real sorrow or repentance behind it.

entries.title: Acts 8:26
segments:
Gaza. It had been destroyed in 96 BC, but was afterward rebuilt on a site nearer the seacoast.  It was the most southerly of the five principal cities of the Philistines.
 

 
The same is desert. This refers to the desert country on either side of the road to Gaza which Philip was directed to take.

entries.title: Acts 8:27
segments:
Ethiopia. That is, kingdom of Meroe, south of Egypt.
 

 
Candace. Meroe was ruled by queens whose dynastic name was Candace, just as the Egyptian kings of that time were called Ptolemies.
 

 
To Jerusalem to worship. He was a proselyte or convert.

entries.title: Acts 8:32
segments:
,33
 
He was led, etc.  The Servant of Jehovah, whose sufferings are described in these verses, is identified with Jesus Christ in

.
 

 
In his humiliation. He was cruelly prejudged, and thus humiliated, but the Jew; he was carelessly considered, and thus humiliated, by The Jew; he was carelessly considered, and thus humiliated, by the Roman.
 

 
His judgment was taken away. That is, justice was denied him by the bitter prejudice of the Sanhedrin and the weakness and dishonesty of Pilate.
 

 
His generation. The contemporaries of Jesus. By 'who shall declare' is meant that it would be difficult adequately to describe the wickedness of those who were resolved upon his death.
 

 
His life is taken from the earth. That is, he was put to death on the cross.

entries.title: Acts 8:36
segments:
As they went on the way. It took time and great discretion for Philip to impart the necessary instruction.  Most probably his eminent pupil had already heard much about Jesus and the new sect, for he had likely been in Jerusalem before; but Jewish sources of information would be prejudiced and Philip had to correct wrong notions.  It is clear that Philip told him not only about the life and death and general teaching of Jesus, but explained the sacrament of baptism, and, most probably, that of the Lord's Supper.
 

 
To be baptized. That every doubt had been removed is hereby shown.

entries.title: Acts 8:39
segments: Caught away Philip That is, most probably, inspired him suddenly to leave to continue his work elsewhere, beginning at Azotus.

entries.title: Acts 8:40
segments:
Azotus. One of the five principal Philistine cities.  It was twenty miles north of Gaza.
 

 
All the cities. Including Jamnia, Joppa and Lydda.
 

 
Caesarea. A city on the coast of Palestine.  It was built by Herod the Great in 12 BC on the site of a small town called Strato's Tower and renamed Caesarea Augusta after Augustus Caesar.  It was an important city until about 1300 AD.  Its inhabitants were chiefly Greeks and Jews.  After 6 AD it became the residence of the Roman procurators, whose authority extended over all Palestine.
